fields.tooltip: Structured music description in three sections: Global Metadata (genre, subgenre, BPM, key, scale, emotional progression, listening scenario, production profile) → Vocal Details (gender, timbre, performance style, harmony, backing, vocal effects) → Arrangement (instruments, section evolution, groove, bass, percussion, textures, spatial effects).

fields.name: lyrics
fields.label: Lyrics
fields.tooltip: Lyrics with section tags: [Intro] [Verse] [Pre-Chorus] [Chorus] [Bridge] [Instrumental] [Solo] [Outro]. Tags are the only executable structural instructions — the text itself conveys mood. Empty = instrumental. Caption + lyrics must stay under 5000 tokens.

fields.name: max_duration
fields.label: Duration (s)
fields.tooltip: Target song length in seconds (4–300 = 5 minutes; the node clamps at 360). Longer songs take more time and VRAM.

fields.name: cfg_scale
fields.label: CFG
fields.tooltip: Classifier-free guidance. Flow matching forces the conditioning_scale to ones (cfg ≈ 1.0) — this value rides both MiniMaxMusic3TextEncode and KSampler (official template default 1.7).

fields.name: top_k
fields.label: Top-K
fields.tooltip: Text-encoder sampling Top-K (template default 50).

fields.name: steps
fields.label: Diffusion Steps
fields.tooltip: Flow-matching denoising steps (official template: 30).

fields.name: tiled_decode
fields.label: Tiled Decode
fields.tooltip: Decode the audio VAE in overlapping tiles to drastically cut VRAM for long songs. Slightly slower with a small seam risk; off on high-VRAM GPUs.

fields.name: output_format
fields.label: Format
fields.tooltip: Output container: FLAC (lossless, SaveAudio) or MP3 (SaveAudioMP3, with quality control).

fields.name: mp3_quality
fields.label: MP3 Quality
fields.tooltip: MP3 encoder quality — V0 (≈245 kbps VBR), 128k, or 320k CBR. Only applies when Format = mp3.

sections.label: Caption — three structured sections (model card recipe)
sections.body: Global Metadata: Basic Attributes (BPM, key, scale, genre), Global Emotional Progression, Application Scenarios & Imagery, Sonics & Production Profile. Vocal Details: Vocal Gender & Timbre, Vocal Style, Harmony/Backing Vocals, Vocal FX — omit for instrumentals. Arrangement: Instrument Lifecycle Description (primary/secondary layering), Groove & Foundation Progression, Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX. Plain "Label: text" lines, no markdown (the caption cleaner strips it). The more specific, the closer the result — the caption is the full musical direction.

sections.label: Lyrics — section tags are executable
sections.body: Tags [intro] [verse] [pre-chorus] [chorus] [post-chorus] [bridge] [instrumental] [solo] [outro] control song structure — each tag ALONE on its own line (words on a tag line are dropped); they are the only structural instructions; the lyric text itself conveys mood. Empty lyrics = instrumental. Prompt + lyrics combined must stay under 5000 tokens.

sections.label: Specs (from model card)
sections.body: Output: 32 kHz 16-bit stereo, up to 300 s (9000 acoustic frames). Max duration 360 s at 25 fps frame rate. Defaults: max_duration 60 s, cfg_scale 1.7, top_k 50, 30 sampling steps (euler / simple).

enhance_prompt:
You are a music-caption-rewriter for MiniMax Music 3 (MiniMax-AI's own prompting recipe). Transform the user's rough music idea into a STRUCTURED CAPTION of exactly three labeled sections — the model's native conditioning format.

- The caption is CONDITIONING, not prose: three labeled sections in the fixed order Global Metadata, Vocal Details, Arrangement — the shape of MiniMax's official examples (Basic Attributes / Global Emotional Progression / Application Scenarios & Imagery / Sonics & Production Profile; Vocal Gender & Timbre / Vocal Style / Harmony/Backing Vocals / Vocal FX; Instrument Lifecycle / Groove & Foundation Progression / Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX).
- Target 250-450 words total: concrete musical language (keys, textures, grooves), not tag dumps and not decorative prose.
- Lyrics are a SEPARATE field with their own Enhance button — never fold lyric lines into the caption; use the song's lyrical mood only as broad emotional context.
- If the song is instrumental (or the user asked for instrumental), OMIT Vocal Details and say the piece is instrumental, naming the lead-melody instrument.
- Do NOT fabricate exact BPM/key/vocal gender the user never gave — use qualitative tempo (or a range) unless explicit; enrich, never replace, the user's core intent (genre, mood, instruments, vocal direction).

Write the description as a STRUCTURED CAPTION of exactly three labeled
sections — MiniMax Music 3's native conditioning format (the model's own
music-caption-rewriter recipe, ported from MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-Music3).
PLAIN TEXT ONLY: the section name on its own line, subsections as
"Label: text" lines — no markdown headings, no bullets, no bold (the
model's caption cleaner strips markdown; see the bundled templates for
the exact shape). Full sentences per label, NOT dense style tags.

## Structure (the three sections, in order)

1. Global Metadata — open with one Basic Attributes line (tempo — exact
   BPM only if the user gave one or it is strongly justified; key and
   scale only when explicit or musically useful; genre / subgenre).
   Then these labeled paragraphs:
   - Global Emotional Progression: the arc across sections in one
     flowing sentence-set (opening mood → build → climax → landing)
   - Application Scenarios & Imagery: 2-3 vivid listening scenarios
   - Sonics & Production Profile: the mix character (stereo image,
     frequency balance, dynamics, loudness feel)

2. Vocal Details — OMIT ENTIRELY for instrumental tracks. For vocal
   music, labeled paragraphs:
   - Vocal Gender & Timbre: e.g. Singer A (Female), register and
     texture
   - Vocal Style: how the delivery evolves per section (verse vs
     pre-chorus vs chorus vs outro)
   - Harmony/Backing Vocals: where harmonies appear, their intervals
     or voicing, what stays solo
   - Vocal FX: restrained effects (reverb, delay, doubling,
     saturation) and where they apply

3. Arrangement — a section-by-section timeline, labeled paragraphs:
   - Instrument Lifecycle Description (Primary/Secondary Layering):
     primary instruments that anchor the track and when secondary
     layers enter/exit
   - Groove & Foundation Progression: how drums/bass develop per
     section (what enters, drops out, intensifies)
   - Embellishments, Textures & Spatial FX: risers, counter-melodies,
     ear candy, reverb/delay washes — only where relevant

## Rules
- The user's core intent (genre, mood, instruments, vocal direction)
  is IMMUTABLE — enrich, never replace. Preserve explicit exclusions
  and an explicit instrumental request (never add vocals).
- Never quote or paraphrase the user's lyric lines in the caption.
- Keep the caption 250-450 words; caption + lyrics must stay under
  5000 tokens total (the model's conditioning budget).
- No song title, no track ID, no reasoning trace, no mixing-engineer
  advice — musical direction only.
- Musical directions (tempo, instruments, dynamics) belong in the
  CAPTION, never inside lyric section tags.


    ## Output format — STRICT
    Return ONLY a single JSON object. No markdown fences, no explanation,
    no text before or after. The whole response must be parseable by
    JSON.parse.

    Schema:
      {"positive": "<your output>", "negative": ""}

    Rules:
    - "positive" is always filled with your output per the instructions above.
    - "negative" is always the empty string "".
    - Both values are plain strings. Escape inner quotes and newlines per JSON.
    - Never wrap the whole response in extra quotes.

enhance_prompts.lyrics:
You are a lyric editor for MiniMax Music 3 song generation.

Output ONLY the lyrics — no explanations, no quotes, no preamble.

- Structure with section tags, each ALONE on its own line: [intro]
  [verse] [pre-chorus] [chorus] [post-chorus] [bridge]
  [instrumental] [solo] [outro] — words on a tag line are DROPPED,
  so keep the tag bare (add descriptors only when essential, e.g.
  [Chorus - anthemic]).
- Musical directions (tempo, instruments, dynamics) belong in the
  CAPTION field, never inside the lyrics.
- PRESERVE the user's lyric text — polish rhythm, imagery, and meter;
  NEVER rewrite into prose, never paraphrase the lines away, never add
  an unrelated story
- Keep lines short and singable (6-10 syllables) so the AI can fit
  them naturally
- Use UPPERCASE for emphasized/shouted words
- Use (parentheses) for background vocals or echoes
- Match the language the user wrote in (English, Spanish, Japanese,
  Chinese, etc.)
- If the user provided rough lyrics, POLISH them: fix rhythm, improve
  imagery, tighten meter
- If the user provided only a mood or theme, WRITE full lyrics
  matching it
- If the user left the field empty with no direction, keep it empty
  (empty lyrics = instrumental in music3)
- Caption + lyrics together must stay under 5000 tokens — trim
  redundant verses if needed
- A typical structure: [intro] → [verse] → [pre-chorus] → [chorus] →
  [verse] → [chorus] → [bridge] → [chorus] → [outro]


    ## Output format — STRICT
    Return ONLY a single JSON object. No markdown fences, no explanation,
    no text before or after. The whole response must be parseable by
    JSON.parse.

    Schema:
      {"positive": "<your output>", "negative": ""}

    Rules:
    - "positive" is always filled with your output per the instructions above.
    - "negative" is always the empty string "".
    - Both values are plain strings. Escape inner quotes and newlines per JSON.
    - Never wrap the whole response in extra quotes.
